hero.headline: US military strikes Iranian radar sites after drone launches toward Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
The US military struck Iranian coastal radar sites and shot down at least four Iranian drones after Iran launched drones toward the Strait of Hormuz, according to US military officials. The strikes targeted radar installations along Iran's southern coast following the drone launches in the strategic waterway through which much of the world's oil passes.

The confrontation represents a significant escalation in tensions between the United States and Iran. US forces intercepted the Iranian drones before they could reach their intended targets in the strait. The military characterized the strikes on radar sites as defensive measures taken to protect shipping lanes and US interests in the region.

Reports indicate that Kuwait and Bahrain also came under attack during the flare-up, though details about those incidents remain limited. The Strait of Hormuz serves as a critical chokepoint for global energy supplies, with roughly one-fifth of the world's petroleum passing through the narrow waterway between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula.

The strikes come amid broader regional tensions and ongoing uncertainty surrounding US-Iran diplomatic talks. Iran has previously threatened to disrupt shipping through the strait during periods of heightened conflict with Western powers. The US maintains a significant naval presence in the Persian Gulf to ensure freedom of navigation through the waterway.

The timing of the incident adds another layer of complexity to the regional security situation, occurring as Israel continues military operations in southern Lebanon and as diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions face obstacles. US military officials have not provided details about the extent of damage to Iranian facilities or whether there were any casualties from the American strikes.

cards.headline: Israel strikes southern Lebanon after evacuating nine villages
cards.teaser: Israel ordered evacuations of nine villages in southern Lebanon before conducting new strikes in the region.
cards.body:
Israel conducted military strikes in southern Lebanon after ordering evacuations from nine villages in the region. The United States announced a ceasefire agreement following diplomatic talks, but Hezbollah rejected the plan.

The conflict has caused severe humanitarian consequences, with 2,900 people killed, 36,000 homes destroyed, and 1.4 million residents displaced. A UN peacekeeper was killed and others wounded when they came under mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon.

cards.headline: Putin declines meeting with Zelenskyy, says he sees no reason for talks
cards.teaser: Russian President Vladimir Putin rejected Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's call for face-to-face peace negotiations.
cards.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has rejected Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's offer for face-to-face talks, saying he currently sees "no point" in meeting. Putin made the comments at the St. Petersburg economic forum while describing Zelenskyy's open letter as rude. He refused to use Zelenskyy's name when responding to questions about the possibility of discussing an end to the conflict.

Putin reaffirmed Russia's intention to achieve its war objectives in Ukraine, including seizing all of the eastern Donbas region. His remarks signal a continued commitment to military operations rather than pursuing immediate diplomatic negotiations with the Ukrainian leadership.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Suffer Worst Single-Day Drop of 2026 After Strong Jobs Report
cards.teaser: U.S.
cards.body:
U.S. stock markets fell sharply on Friday, with the S&P 500 declining more than 2.6 percent in its worst single-day performance of the year, ending a nine-week winning streak. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 695 points, while the Nasdaq Composite plunged 4 percent, its steepest fall since April 2025.

The selloff followed stronger-than-expected jobs data, prompting investors to reassess expectations for Federal Reserve policy. Treasury yields jumped as traders increased bets that the central bank would maintain higher interest rates rather than cutting them. Technology stocks led the market downturn, with semiconductor manufacturers and artificial intelligence companies experiencing significant losses after weeks of substantial gains.

cards.headline: Department of Homeland Security whistleblower alleges plan to mark 2.7 million living people as dead
cards.teaser: A whistleblower claims an immigration enforcement initiative would have incorrectly designated millions of living individuals as deceased.
cards.body:
A Department of Homeland Security whistleblower has alleged that a plan connected to immigration enforcement efforts would have marked 2.7 million living people as deceased in government records. The whistleblower came forward with allegations about the proposal, which they say was part of a broader immigration enforcement push.

The allegations raise questions about data accuracy and potential consequences for individuals who might have been incorrectly marked as dead in federal systems. Such designations could affect access to government services, financial accounts, and legal status.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Considers Taking Equity Stakes in AI Companies
cards.teaser: The administration is exploring government partnerships with artificial intelligence firms, including possible equity positions.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump said the U.S. government may take equity stakes in artificial intelligence companies, according to reports. The Trump administration is in discussions with OpenAI and other AI startups about possible government ownership positions as part of a broader partnership strategy.

Trump indicated he could meet with artificial intelligence companies as soon as next week to discuss a government profit-sharing plan. The proposal would involve the U.S. government treating AI development as a public resource in exchange for financial participation. The discussions represent a significant shift in how the federal government might engage with the artificial intelligence industry.

cards.headline: France investigates alleged Israeli mistreatment of pro-Palestinian flotilla activists
cards.teaser: French authorities opened an investigation into claims that activists detained with a Gaza-bound flotilla were abused in Israeli custody.
cards.body:
France has launched an investigation into allegations that Israeli authorities mistreated pro-Palestinian flotilla activists who were detained while attempting to reach Gaza. The activists have reported abuse during their custody.

Israeli authorities have denied the mistreatment allegations. The flotilla was intercepted before reaching Gaza, and participants were taken into Israeli custody.

cards.headline: Protests continue in Albania over Kushner-linked luxury resort plan
cards.teaser: Demonstrations have grown over a planned luxury resort near a protected wetland backed by Jared Kushner, son-in-law of former President Trump.
cards.body:
Thousands of demonstrators have taken to the streets of Tirana this week opposing a $1.6 billion luxury resort backed by Jared Kushner. The complex is planned in an environmentally sensitive Mediterranean area that is home to 200 bird species, including flamingos and Dalmatian pelicans.

Construction crews have begun erecting fences around the site, triggering public outrage over environmental damage and concerns about political transparency surrounding the project. Albania's prime minister defended the development, suggesting opposition is driven primarily by Kushner's involvement rather than the project itself.

cards.headline: Iran's soccer team receives US visas days before World Cup starts
cards.teaser: Iranian players were granted entry to the United States just days before the World Cup begins, ending months of uncertainty.
cards.body:
Iran's national soccer team received visas to compete in the World Cup just days before the tournament began, ending months of uncertainty about their participation. However, many of the team's staff members were denied entry to the United States.

The last-minute visa approvals allowed Iran to field a team for the competition, though the denial of visas for numerous support staff meant the team would operate with reduced resources during the event.

cards.headline: Astronauts return to ISS main section after air leak repair attempt
cards.teaser: Five astronauts sheltered in a safe area of the International Space Station while Russian crew members attempted to repair an air leak.
cards.body:
Five astronauts aboard the International Space Station returned to the main station after sheltering during repair work on an air leak. The safe-haven procedure was implemented as a precautionary measure while Russian crew members worked on the issue.

Roscosmos reported that two air leaks were discovered in the Zveza module's transfer chamber during pressurization tests. Specialists detected the leaks while pressurizing the chamber connecting to the ISS, prompting NASA to order the five crew members to prepare for a possible evacuation before clearing them to return once repair efforts were paused.

hero.headline: Federal prosecutors open investigations into California election administration
hero.body:
The United States Attorney's Office has launched investigations into California's election processes and deployed a prosecutor to a Los Angeles vote center. The announcement came as millions of ballots remained uncounted in the state's primary election.

The decision to send federal prosecutors to observe election administration represents an unusual level of federal involvement in state election operations. The investigations target unspecified aspects of how California conducted its primary voting, which concluded this week.

California uses a top-two primary system in which all candidates appear on a single ballot regardless of party, with the top two vote-getters advancing to the November general election. The state allows mail-in ballots postmarked by election day to be counted for days afterward, a practice that typically means results take longer to finalize than in states with different ballot-counting rules.

The U.S. Attorney's Office has not publicly detailed what prompted the investigations or what specific election procedures are under scrutiny. Federal prosecutors have authority to investigate potential violations of federal voting rights laws, but state and local officials typically manage election administration with minimal federal intervention.

The deployment of a prosecutor to a Los Angeles vote center suggests federal officials are monitoring ongoing ballot processing. Los Angeles County, the nation's most populous county, processes millions of ballots and has historically taken weeks to complete its count. The presence of federal observers at vote-counting locations is rare outside of areas with histories of voting rights violations.

cards.headline: National Park Service ranger dies in crevasse fall on Mount McKinley
cards.teaser: A climbing ranger fell into a crevasse while on patrol on the mountain, marking the fourth death of the season on the peak.
cards.body:
A National Park Service ranger died after falling into a crevasse on Mount McKinley, the park service announced. The ranger was conducting a patrol on the mountain at the time of the accident.

The death marks the fourth fatality of the current climbing season on Mount McKinley, the tallest peak in North America. The park service has not released the ranger's name or additional details about the circumstances of the fall.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra secures top position in California governor primary
cards.teaser: The former Health and Human Services Secretary won the most votes in the state's primary election, advancing to the November general election.
cards.body:
Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra has secured the top spot on California's gubernatorial ballot, advancing to the November general election. His come-from-behind primary victory emerged from a crowded Democratic field competing to succeed Governor Gavin Newsom.

With millions of ballots still being counted, Becerra's general election opponent remains undetermined. He could face Democrat Tom Steyer, an environmental activist backing progressive policies including universal healthcare and higher taxes on billionaires, or Republican Steve Hilton, a former UK political operative and Fox News personality endorsed by Donald Trump.

cards.headline: Virginia man sentenced to life in prison for wife's murder
cards.teaser: Brendan Banfield received a life sentence for plotting with his family's au pair to kill his wife during an affair.
cards.body:
A Virginia man was sentenced to life in prison without parole for murdering his wife and another man. Brendan Banfield, a former IRS law enforcement officer, was convicted of killing Christine Banfield, a pediatric intensive care nurse, and Joseph Ryan on February 24, 2023.

Banfield carried out the murders with his family's Brazilian au pair, Juliana Peres Magalhães, with whom he was having an affair. Prosecutors said the pair lured Ryan to their home as a fall guy for the crime. Banfield claimed he shot Ryan in self-defense after discovering him attacking his wife, but the court rejected this account.

cards.headline: Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner faces renewed scrutiny ahead of primary
cards.teaser: The Democratic Senate candidate confronts additional questions about past behavior as supporters urge an apology to women who alleged disturbing conduct.
cards.body:
Graham Platner is confronting fresh scrutiny as Maine's Senate primary approaches. Women have alleged disturbing behavior by the candidate, and Representative Ro Khanna has called on Platner to apologize to his accusers. A recent New York Times report documented accusations that Platner was physically rough with former girlfriends.

Platner denies the allegations and characterizes the controversies as signs his campaign is gaining traction. Some Democrats have expressed concern about his candidacy, while one accuser suggested the recent reporting may actually benefit Platner's Senate bid.

cards.headline: Los Angeles mayoral race tightens as votes continue to be counted
cards.teaser: Councilmember Nithya Raman narrowed the gap with Spencer Pratt in the contest to advance to the November runoff against incumbent Karen Bass.
cards.body:
Nithya Raman narrowed her gap with Spencer Pratt in the Los Angeles mayoral primary's race for second place. As of Friday's ballot count, Raman trailed Pratt by approximately 20,672 votes.

The top two finishers advance to face Mayor Karen Bass in November's general election. Millions of ballots remained to be counted across Los Angeles County as vote processing continued.

cards.headline: Sesame Street character draws criticism over NBA Finals support
cards.teaser: Elmo faced backlash from New Yorkers after failing to fully support the Knicks in the basketball championship series.
cards.body:
The Sesame Street character Elmo faced backlash from New York residents after failing to fully support the Knicks in the NBA Finals. Given that Elmo's fictional home is located in New York, fans expected stronger backing for the city's basketball team.

The criticism reflects the deep passion New York sports enthusiasts have for their local teams and the figures associated with the city. Many residents view public personalities and institutions as having a responsibility to champion the city's representatives in major sporting events.

hero.headline: Google Agrees to Pay SpaceX Nearly $1 Billion Monthly for Cloud Computing
hero.teaser: Google secured a massive cloud computing deal with SpaceX worth approximately $920 million per month.
hero.body:
Google has reached an agreement to pay SpaceX approximately $920 million per month for computing capacity at xAI data centers, according to multiple reports. The arrangement represents a $30 billion total commitment and comes as SpaceX prepares for its initial public offering.

The deal provides Google with artificial intelligence computing power to support recently launched AI products. A Google representative attributed the contract to unexpected demand for these new offerings. The agreement positions SpaceX as a major provider of computing infrastructure for technology companies developing AI systems.

This follows a similar arrangement SpaceX previously signed with Anthropic for AI compute capacity. The contracts highlight growing demand from tech firms for dedicated computing resources as they scale artificial intelligence applications.

SpaceX is preparing for what could become the largest initial public offering in history. The company is targeting a $75 billion fundraising, which would value it at approximately $1.77 trillion. The IPO is scheduled for mid-June.

SpaceX operates as a sprawling conglomerate encompassing multiple divisions. Its space segment handles rocket launches for clients including NASA. The connectivity division manages Starlink, its satellite broadband service. The AI division oversees xAI and the social media platform X, formerly Twitter.

The company faces significant financial challenges despite revenue growth. SpaceX reported a $4.9 billion loss in 2025 on revenues of $18.7 billion, though revenue increased by one-third compared to 2024. Losses have accelerated this year, with a $4.3 billion loss in the first quarter compared to a $528 million loss in the same period last year.

The connectivity segment generates the most revenue at $11.4 billion, followed by the space division at $4.1 billion and the AI unit at $3.2 billion. However, only the connectivity division was profitable during the first three months of this year. The AI unit is heavily loss-making, having lost $6.4 billion last year due to higher computing expenses required to build and operate AI models.

Capital expenditure totaled $20.7 billion, with the xAI unit accounting for $12.7 billion, primarily for constructing massive data centers. SpaceX has built a facility called the Colossus data center to support these operations.

Founder and CEO Elon Musk will maintain approximately 85 percent voting control of SpaceX through majority ownership of Class B shares, which carry 10 votes per share compared to one vote for Class A shares held by other investors. Musk's base salary remains unchanged at $54,000 annually since 2019.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Suffer Worst Single-Day Drop of 2026 After Strong Jobs Report
cards.teaser: U.S.
cards.body:
U.S. stock markets fell sharply on Friday, with the S&P 500 declining more than 2.6 percent in its worst single-day performance of the year, ending a nine-week winning streak. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 695 points, while the Nasdaq Composite plunged 4 percent, its steepest fall since April 2025.

The selloff followed stronger-than-expected jobs data, prompting investors to reassess expectations for Federal Reserve policy. Treasury yields jumped as traders increased bets that the central bank would maintain higher interest rates rather than cutting them. Technology stocks led the market downturn, with semiconductor manufacturers and artificial intelligence companies experiencing significant losses after weeks of substantial gains.

cards.headline: U.S. States Prepare Lawsuit to Block Paramount Acquisition of Warner Bros.
cards.teaser: Multiple state attorneys general are planning legal action to prevent Paramount from acquiring Warner Bros. on antitrust grounds.
cards.body:
U.S. state officials are preparing a lawsuit to block Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros., according to sources. At least 10 states are considering joining the antitrust challenge, with California expected to decide soon whether it will participate in the effort to prevent the merger.

Paramount has pushed back against opposition to the deal, with company lawyers claiming that some opponents hold antisemitic views. The company characterized the lawsuit as a clumsy attempt to politicize antitrust litigation. The merger faces scrutiny over concerns about market concentration in the entertainment industry.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Considers Taking Equity Stakes in AI Companies
cards.teaser: The administration is exploring government partnerships with artificial intelligence firms, including possible equity positions.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump said the U.S. government may take equity stakes in artificial intelligence companies, according to reports. The Trump administration is in discussions with OpenAI and other AI startups about possible government ownership positions as part of a broader partnership strategy.

The proposal would involve the U.S. government treating AI development as a public resource in exchange for financial participation. The discussions represent a significant shift in how the federal government might engage with the artificial intelligence industry.

cards.headline: Bitcoin Falls Below $60,000 to Lowest Level Since October 2024
cards.teaser: The cryptocurrency dropped sharply following strong jobs data and technical issues with another digital currency.
cards.body:
Bitcoin dropped below $60,000 on Friday, marking its lowest price since October 2024. The decline erased billions in value from cryptocurrency positions as the market faced mounting pressure.

The sell-off followed a strong U.S. jobs report that heightened expectations for higher interest rates. A software bug affecting Zcash added to broader weakness across digital currencies. The cryptocurrency market also faced headwinds from investors rotating toward artificial intelligence stocks and technology company IPOs.

cards.headline: SpaceX Faces Extended Wait for S&P 500 Index Inclusion
cards.teaser: The company's financial losses may delay its entry into the benchmark stock index even after a planned IPO.
cards.body:
SpaceX will likely wait years to join the S&P 500 index following its anticipated initial public offering, according to analysts. The company operates at a significant financial loss, which creates obstacles for inclusion in the benchmark stock index that tracks 500 large U.S. companies.

The S&P 500's rejection of SpaceX also affects other large private companies including OpenAI and Anthropic, which face similar barriers to index membership. Companies must meet profitability requirements and other criteria to qualify for the index. Despite its valuation and market presence, SpaceX's financial performance does not currently align with S&P 500 standards.

cards.headline: Advanced Nuclear Reactor Reaches Critical Development Milestone
cards.teaser: The Energy Department announced the first advanced nuclear reactor to achieve a significant technical benchmark.
cards.body:
An advanced nuclear reactor has become the first to reach a critical milestone in its development, the Energy Department announced. The achievement marks progress in next-generation nuclear energy technology.

The milestone represents an advancement in efforts to develop new types of nuclear reactors that differ from traditional designs. The Energy Department has been supporting research and development of advanced reactor concepts as part of broader energy initiatives.

hero.headline: Researchers discover exploit allowing hackers to take over PCs through USB-connected Bluetooth speakers
hero.body:
Security researchers have discovered a vulnerability in Creative's USB-connected Bluetooth speakers that allows nearby attackers to take control of connected computers without any user interaction. The exploit, dubbed 'Pwnd Blaster,' takes advantage of how these speakers connect to PCs via USB while simultaneously maintaining Bluetooth connectivity.

The attack works by exploiting the dual connectivity of the speakers. When a Creative speaker is plugged into a PC via USB, it also broadcasts a Bluetooth signal that can be detected by nearby devices. Researchers found they could send specially crafted Bluetooth commands to the speaker that would then be relayed to the connected PC through the USB connection, effectively bypassing normal security controls that would prevent unauthorized Bluetooth access to the computer.

The vulnerability is particularly concerning because it requires no action from the victim. Traditional attacks typically require users to click a malicious link, download infected software, or accept a connection request. In this case, simply having the speaker connected to a PC and powered on creates an attack surface that hackers within Bluetooth range can exploit to gain system access.

The discovery has prompted alarm among PC security professionals and users. The revelation that common peripheral devices can serve as entry points for attacks represents a blind spot in typical security practices. Most users focus on protecting their systems from network-based threats or malicious software, but rarely consider that accessories like speakers could provide attackers with a pathway to compromise their machines.

Creative has not yet issued a public statement about the vulnerability or announced plans for a firmware update to address the issue. Security experts recommend that users concerned about the exploit either disconnect affected speakers when not in use or disable their Bluetooth functionality if possible. The research highlights the growing challenge of securing computers as peripheral devices become more sophisticated and incorporate multiple connectivity methods that can interact in unexpected ways.

cards.headline: Food and Drug Administration continues investigating baby botulism outbreak without identified cause
cards.teaser: Federal health officials are still working to determine the source of a botulism outbreak affecting infants.
cards.body:
The FDA is still searching for the source of an ongoing baby botulism outbreak. Three companies involved in the investigation have blamed each other for the contamination, but no definitive cause has emerged.

Infant botulism is a serious condition caused by toxins that damage the nervous system. Young children who contract the illness require immediate medical care.

cards.headline: Astronauts return to International Space Station after sheltering during Russian air leak repair
cards.teaser: Five astronauts moved back to their regular areas of the ISS following a Russian repair attempt on a tunnel leak.
cards.body:
Astronauts aboard the International Space Station have resumed normal duties after being placed on evacuation alert due to air leaks in the Russian segment. NASA ordered four astronauts from the Crew-12 mission to enter their docked Crew Dragon spacecraft and don spacesuits as a precaution while specialists assessed the situation.

Russian specialists discovered two air leaks while pressurizing the transfer chamber of the Zveda module. After repair efforts were paused, NASA cleared the crew to return to their regular operations aboard the orbiting laboratory.

cards.headline: LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman leaves Microsoft board to focus on AI drug discovery startup
cards.teaser: Reid Hoffman is stepping down from Microsoft's board after a decade to dedicate time to Manus, his artificial intelligence company.
cards.body:
Reid Hoffman has stepped down from Microsoft's board after a decade of service to focus on Manus, his AI drug discovery startup. His departure marks a shift toward what he calls "founder mode," taking a more direct role in building the company rather than serving on boards of established corporations.

Hoffman's exit comes after a profitable tenure at Microsoft, during which he benefited from the company's growth and success.

cards.headline: Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy to conclude with Revelation in spring 2027
cards.teaser: Square Enix announced the third and final installment of its Final Fantasy VII remake series will launch next year.
cards.body:
Square Enix has officially announced Final Fantasy VII: Revelation, the third and final installment in its remake trilogy of the original 1997 game. The publisher unveiled a first trailer for the title at Summer Game Fest Live.

The game will launch simultaneously across PC, PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2 in spring 2027. Screenshots demonstrating the game running on Switch 2 hardware were also released alongside the announcement.

cards.headline: Founders share negative experiences with venture capitalists in viral social media thread
cards.teaser: Startup founders have been posting stories about problematic interactions with venture capital investors, with some identifying specific firms.
cards.body:
A large conversation on social media platform X has seen founders sharing stories about negative experiences with venture capital firms and individual investors. Some participants in the discussion have named specific VCs and firms in their accounts.

The stories range from unusual behavior to what founders describe as frustrating interactions during fundraising processes. The viral thread has drawn attention to the power dynamics and relationship challenges that can emerge between startups seeking funding and the investors who control access to capital.

cards.headline: Guild Wars 3 announced for PC and PlayStation 5 with beta planned for next year
cards.teaser: ArenaNet unveiled the third installment in the Guild Wars online game series at Summer Game Fest.
cards.body:
Guild Wars 3 was announced at Summer Game Fest for release on PC and PlayStation 5. Developer ArenaNet described the game as a modern evolution of the massively multiplayer online role-playing game genre and confirmed a beta test is scheduled for next year.

The game is set 1,000 years before the events of the original Guild Wars. ArenaNet also addressed the future of Guild Wars 2, though specific details about how both games will coexist were not provided in the announcement.

hero.headline: Knicks lead Spurs at halftime in Game 2 of NBA Finals
hero.body:
The New York Knicks hold a halftime lead over the San Antonio Spurs in Game 2 of the NBA Finals at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio. The matchup represents a crucial contest as both teams battle for control of the championship series.

Karl-Anthony Towns has emerged as the standout performer through the first half, scoring 17 points in 18 minutes while also contributing seven rebounds, three assists, a steal and a block. His strong play has helped the Knicks build their advantage and has been instrumental in containing Victor Wembanyama, who has managed just seven points on 2-for-4 shooting through two quarters. Wembanyama does have five rebounds and two blocks.

Mikal Bridges continues his strong playoff performance, shooting 4-for-5 for 11 points. Jalen Brunson, despite some shooting struggles, has 10 points on 3-for-11 shooting to go along with two steals. For San Antonio, De'Aaron Fox leads the scoring with 12 points, while Devin Vassell adds 11 points.

The officiating has drawn attention at times during the game, with several questionable calls affecting the flow of play. One sequence saw Towns called for an offensive foul that drew criticism from observers, as replays appeared to show he was being held before freeing himself.

Wembanyama's performance will be critical for the Spurs moving forward. The 7-foot-4 center needs to deliver on both ends of the floor to help San Antonio stay competitive in this series. His ability to impact the game defensively and provide scoring will be essential as the Spurs look to prevent the Knicks from taking control of the Finals.

Game 3 is scheduled to take place at Madison Square Garden in New York. President Donald Trump has accepted an invitation to attend the game, prompting heightened security measures at the venue. The NBA has implemented a ban on all bags at Madison Square Garden for the event. Knicks center Mitchell Robinson has expressed enthusiasm about the opportunity to play in front of the president.

The series carries significant weight for both franchises. The Knicks are pursuing their first championship in 53 years, while the Spurs aim to add another title to their storied history. The outcome of Game 2 will determine whether San Antonio can tie the series or if New York will take a commanding lead heading into their home games in Manhattan.

The game tips off at 8:30 p.m. ET from the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio as the two teams continue their battle for NBA supremacy.

cards.headline: Giants rout Cubs 18-3 behind Chapman's eight-RBI performance
cards.teaser: The San Francisco Giants defeated the Chicago Cubs 18-3, with Matt Chapman hitting a grand slam and driving in eight runs.
cards.body:
Matt Chapman powered the San Francisco Giants to an 18-3 victory over the Chicago Cubs, hitting a grand slam and totaling eight RBIs in the lopsided game. Willy Adames also contributed with a home run that landed on Waveland Avenue, giving the Giants an early lead.

Cubs pitcher Edward Cabrera struggled on the mound, surrendering three home runs as Chicago suffered a decisive defeat. The loss erased any cautious optimism the Cubs had built heading into the game against San Francisco.

cards.headline: England suffers heaviest defeat in 17 years against Spain
cards.teaser: England lost heavily to Spain in what marks their worst defeat since 2009, though the team only needed to avoid a loss.
cards.body:
England suffered their heaviest defeat in 17 years against Spain. The loss was particularly disappointing given that the team's objective was simply to avoid defeat in the match.

Despite the disappointing result, experts believe there is no need for panic at this stage. The team will need to analyze their performance and work to address the weaknesses that Spain's play exposed during the game.

cards.headline: Rangers activate Corey Seager and Wyatt Langford, designate Sam Haggerty
cards.teaser: The Texas Rangers activated Corey Seager and Wyatt Langford from the injured list while designating Sam Haggerty for assignment.
cards.body:
The Texas Rangers activated shortstop Corey Seager and outfielder Wyatt Langford from the injured list. Seager had been sidelined with a back injury while Langford was recovering from a forearm injury. Both players returned to the lineup against the Cleveland Guardians.

To make space on the roster, the Rangers designated utility player Sam Haggerty for assignment. In his first game back, Seager broke an 0-for-29 slump by hitting a two-run home run.

cards.headline: Gio Ruggiero wins rain-shortened ARCA race at Michigan
cards.teaser: Gio Ruggiero took his third victory of 2026 in the rain-shortened Henry Ford Health 200 at Michigan International Speedway.
cards.body:
Gio Ruggiero earned his third victory of the 2026 season at Michigan International Speedway in the Henry Ford Health 200 ARCA Menards Series race. The event was shortened due to rain that made conditions unsafe for continued competition.

Pole-sitter Cleetus McFarland was involved in a wreck during the race.

cards.headline: FIFA reverses World Cup water bottle ban after backlash
cards.teaser: FIFA announced that fans will be allowed to bring disposable water bottles into World Cup stadiums after reversing an earlier ban.
cards.body:
FIFA reversed its decision to ban disposable water bottles from World Cup stadiums following widespread backlash. The organization initially announced that fans would not be allowed to bring water bottles into games this summer.

New York Mayor Mamdani called the original policy concerning and said he would follow up on the matter. The reversal allows fans to bring water bottles into stadiums during the tournament.

cards.headline: Chicago Bears board votes to advance stadium development in Indiana
cards.teaser: The Chicago Bears board of directors voted to move forward with plans for a new stadium in Hammond, Indiana.
cards.body:
The Chicago Bears board of directors voted to advance development of a new stadium in northwest Indiana, moving the team closer to leaving Chicago. The Bears issued a statement confirming the board's decision to push forward with the Hammond location.

The move has sparked widespread blame in Illinois as officials and residents react to the team's decision. The Bears are moving forward with plans to build their new home across the state line in Indiana.

hero.headline: Actor James Handy Found Stabbed to Death, Girlfriend's Son Charged with Murder
hero.body:
James Handy, an 81-year-old character actor known for roles in films including Top Gun: Maverick and Jumanji, was found stabbed to death outside his home in Tarzana, California. Michael Gledhill, 44, the son of Handy's girlfriend, has been arrested and charged with murder in connection with the killing.

Police discovered Handy unconscious in the front yard of his residence on Wednesday morning at 9:30 a.m. with multiple stab wounds to the chest. He was transported to a hospital where he was later pronounced dead.

According to the Los Angeles police department statement, a 911 caller stated: "I am the son of man, I just killed the man of sin." When officers arrived at the scene, Gledhill told them he was "the one they were looking for." Police noted that the suspect resides at the location with his mother, who is Handy's girlfriend. Gledhill has been held on bail set at 2 million dollars.

Handy built an extensive career as a character actor spanning decades in the entertainment industry. Born in New York City, his television career began in 1977 with the series Ryan's Hope. Beyond his recent work in Top Gun: Maverick, he appeared in numerous films and television programs including Logan, K-911, Law and Order, NCIS: Los Angeles, and Criminal Minds. Top Gun: Maverick, released in 2022, marked his most recent film appearance.

His long career demonstrated his range and reliability in supporting roles across both film and television productions. Handy became a recognizable fixture in Hollywood productions, contributing to major franchises and acclaimed series throughout his professional life.

The incident has drawn attention across the entertainment industry, with colleagues and fans acknowledging his contributions to film and television. His death represents a sudden end to a career that lasted nearly five decades in the entertainment business.

The case is now proceeding through the Los Angeles County criminal justice system as prosecutors move forward with the murder charge against Gledhill. Police continue their investigation into the circumstances surrounding the fatal stabbing.

cards.headline: British Actor Anthony Head Dies at 72
cards.teaser: Anthony Head, the British actor known for his roles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Ted Lasso, has died from complications related to pneumonia.
cards.body:
Anthony Head, the British actor best known for playing Rupert Giles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, has died at age 72 from complications of pneumonia.

Head's career spanned decades and crossed the Atlantic. Beyond Buffy, he appeared in the comedy series Ted Lasso, the BBC fantasy drama Merlin, and the sketch show Little Britain. He first gained public attention in the 1980s through Nescafe advertisements, becoming a recognizable face to audiences in both the UK and US.

cards.headline: Legendary Rock Tattoo Artist Greg James Dies at 71
cards.teaser: Greg James, a tattoo artist who worked with numerous rock musicians throughout his career, has died at age 71.
cards.body:
Greg James, widely known in the music industry for his tattoo artistry, died at 71.

James built a reputation over decades as a go-to tattoo artist for rock musicians and other figures in the entertainment world. His distinctive style and relationships within the rock music community made him a notable figure in both the tattoo and music industries.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift's Toy Story 5 Song Breaks Streaming Records
cards.teaser: A new song by Taylor Swift for the upcoming Toy Story 5 film has broken streaming records and received a music video featuring footage of the character Jessie.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift released a new song for Toy Story 5 featuring the character Jessie, the cowgirl voiced by Joan Cusack. The track marks a return to her country roots and has broken streaming records on Spotify. A music video accompanies the release, showcasing footage of the beloved animated character.

The Guardian praised the song as Swift's best work in years, highlighting its "handcrafted care and rootsy soul." Swift acknowledged the legacy of Randy Newman's iconic Toy Story songs, calling them "incomparable." The collaboration represents a significant moment in her soundtrack ventures, which have historically had limited commercial longevity.

cards.headline: Final Fantasy VII: Revelation Announced as Trilogy Finale for 2027
cards.teaser: Square Enix revealed Final Fantasy VII: Revelation as the third and final game in the remake trilogy, set to launch in spring 2027 across multiple platforms.
cards.body:
Square Enix has officially announced Final Fantasy VII: Revelation as the third and final installment in its Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy. The game will launch in spring 2027 across multiple platforms including PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC.

Square Enix unveiled the first trailer for Revelation during Summer Game Fest Live, giving players a preview of what to expect from the trilogy's conclusion. The release timing aligns with the 30th anniversary of the original Final Fantasy VII game.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce Wedding Rumors Point to Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: Reports suggest Taylor Swift and NFL player Travis Kelce plan to marry at Madison Square Garden in New York City, though official confirmation has not been provided.
cards.body:
Fans worldwide are speculating about a potential wedding between Taylor Swift and Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce. The rumored ceremony would take place in July at Madison Square Garden in New York City with over 1,000 invited guests.

The speculation has drawn attention from major news organizations and even prompted a joking comment from the NYPD commissioner about the rumored New York event. Swifties continue searching for clues about when the couple might marry.

cards.headline: Among Us Animated Series Drops All Episodes on Paramount+
cards.teaser: The animated television adaptation of the video game Among Us released all 10 episodes at once on Paramount+ in a surprise announcement.
cards.body:
Paramount+ released the entire first season of the Among Us animated series without advance notice. The streaming service made all 10 episodes available immediately. Stars Yvette Nicole Brown and Liv Hewson announced the surprise drop at Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles.

The show adapts the popular multiplayer video game Among Us, which became a cultural phenomenon during 2020. The sudden release strategy caught audiences off guard, as there had been limited advance promotion for the series. The show represents Paramount+'s effort to capitalize on the game's popularity and bring its characters and gameplay concepts to television.

hero.headline: Justice Department ends Trump anti-weaponization compensation fund
hero.body:
The Trump administration's nearly $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund will not continue, the Justice Department confirmed in a court filing on Friday. Two DOJ attorneys notified a federal court in the Eastern District of Virginia that the compensation program, established to pay individuals claiming they were targets of government overreach, has been terminated.

The filing came as the Justice Department simultaneously asked the court to dismiss a legal challenge to the fund brought by a former federal prosecutor and several other plaintiffs. The lawsuit had questioned how the fund would operate and who would be eligible for payments.

The fund faced swift legal and political opposition since its announcement last month. U.S. District Judge Leonie Brinkema had temporarily blocked the administration from transferring money from the fund after Democracy Forward filed a lawsuit seeking to dissolve it. The decision to end the program comes just two weeks after it was announced as part of a settlement in the president's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service over the leak of his tax returns.

The compensation program drew intense scrutiny over concerns about lack of oversight and eligibility criteria. Administration officials indicated that payees could include pardoned January 6 rioters, sparking alarm among Republicans and Democrats alike.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune told reporters he believed the best approach would be for the administration to shut the fund down themselves. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called it "corruption in broad daylight" and vowed that Democrats would force Senate Republicans to vote on blocking any payments.

Former Vice President Mike Pence criticized the possibility of compensating Capitol rioters as "deeply offensive," telling NBC's Meet the Press that he believed most Republicans and Americans shared his concern. Several states, including California, Illinois, New York, and Connecticut, proposed tax measures targeting any fund distributions to their residents.

The program also faced criticism over its lack of transparency. The fund's terms did not require disclosure of who received payments or how much they were given. Critics viewed it as a secretive and loosely controlled mechanism that could be used for political favoritism.

The termination of the fund represents a significant reversal for the Trump administration, which had promoted it as a key initiative addressing what supporters characterized as politicized federal law enforcement. The decision appears to reflect the mounting political pressure from both parties concerned about the fund's structure and potential use.

The Justice Department's filing requesting dismissal of the lawsuit means the court has not yet ruled on whether to accept the government's request to end the case now that the program has been discontinued.

cards.headline: Department of Homeland Security whistleblower alleges plan to mark 2.7 million living people as dead
cards.teaser: A whistleblower claims an immigration enforcement initiative would have incorrectly designated millions of living individuals as deceased.
cards.body:
A Department of Homeland Security whistleblower has alleged that a plan connected to immigration enforcement efforts would have marked 2.7 million living people as deceased in government records. The whistleblower came forward with allegations about the proposal, which they say was part of a broader immigration enforcement push.

The allegations raise questions about data accuracy and potential consequences for individuals who might have been incorrectly marked as dead in federal systems. Such designations could affect access to government services, financial accounts, and legal status.

cards.headline: Chief of staff to Texas congressman charged with firearm violations at Capitol
cards.teaser: Luis Vega, who works for Rep. Pete Sessions, faces two counts related to an alleged attempt to bring a gun into the Capitol complex.
cards.body:
Luis Vega, chief of staff to Rep. Pete Sessions of Texas, was charged with two firearm-related counts in connection with an alleged incident at the U.S. Capitol complex. The charges were filed on a Wednesday, months after Vega allegedly attempted to bring a firearm into the Capitol.

The alleged incident occurred in late December of last year. Vega serves as the top staffer for Sessions, a Republican congressman from Texas. The charges represent a rare case of a senior congressional aide facing criminal allegations related to Capitol security violations.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins Democratic primary for New Mexico governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, a former Biden administration official, won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. If elected in the general election, she would become the nation's first female Native American governor.

Haaland previously served in a cabinet position under President Biden before announcing her candidacy for state office.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra takes top spot in California governor primary
cards.teaser: The former Health and Human Services Secretary secured the lead position on November's ballot with millions of votes still being counted.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra, the former Secretary of Health and Human Services, has secured the top spot on California's November ballot for governor. The result comes from the state's primary election, where all candidates compete together regardless of party affiliation, with the two leading vote-getters advancing to the general election.

Becerra's come-from-behind victory marks a significant moment in what has been a turbulent campaign season. Election officials continue counting millions of remaining ballots to determine his general election opponent, who will be either fellow Democrat Tom Steyer or Republican Steve Hilton.

cards.headline: New York legislature passes bills regulating data centers and consumer surveillance pricing
cards.teaser: The state Senate and Assembly approved three measures addressing data center operations, pricing technology, and digital stalking.
cards.body:
The New York State Senate and Assembly passed three bills establishing new regulations for data centers and consumer protections. The legislation addresses data center operations, surveillance-based pricing practices, and digital stalking behaviors.

The bills now await action by Governor Kathy Hochul. Lawmakers did not advance other proposed measures covering environmental policy, housing, and entertainment sectors during the legislative session.

cards.headline: Judge orders former CIA officer accused of gold bar theft to remain in jail
cards.teaser: The court denied release for the defendant while leaving open the possibility of a future hearing if new evidence emerges.
cards.body:
A federal judge has ordered that former CIA officer Rush remain jailed while awaiting trial on theft charges. Prosecutors have described him as a "master manipulator" in connection with allegations involving $40 million in gold bars.

Rush faces charges related to theft of public funds stemming from timesheet claims he allegedly made. The judge indicated that the defense can petition for another hearing if they present new evidence that might support his release.
